budget_items.topic: Verdantis fracture-trace/drilling-site study near 361 Mass Path
budget_items.what_was_said: A hydrogeologist proposed redoing a fracture-trace analysis and staking test sites for a potential bedrock well behind Walmart. The commission discussed the cost of this first step before any decision on drilling.

budget_items.topic: Cost to drill a bedrock test well
budget_items.what_was_said: After the site study, drilling and testing an actual bedrock test well was estimated as a further cost, separate from the site study.
Commissioners compared recent residential well-drilling prices as a reference point for what a test well might cost, disagreeing on what a fair price should be.

budget_items.topic: Casing cost for a test well
budget_items.what_was_said: A commissioner estimated the added cost of casing a well hole, on top of the drilling cost, as a hypothetical total.

budget_items.topic: Pressure-test pump for water main work
budget_items.what_was_said: The superintendent said a pump to pressure-test and chlorinate mains in-house was more expensive than expected, but was not asking for a vote, only flagging it for future purchase.
Commissioners discussed buying a trailer to haul a trench box and other equipment, comparing a flat trailer against a tilt-deck model.
A commissioner said a price quote for equipment (discussed in context of a skid steer) came in higher than expected just before the meeting.

budget_items.topic: Rolling Acres water main: in-house labor vs. contracted cost comparison
budget_items.what_was_said: The superintendent plans to track costs of doing the Rolling Acres work with district crews versus what a contracted/budgeted price would have been, to justify future equipment purchases.

budget_items.topic: Tighe & Bond additional Kedings pH/precipitation pilot study cost
budget_items.what_was_said: A resident and commissioners discussed the cost of an additional pilot study DEP is requiring related to Kedings well water treatment, with the superintendent saying the true cost was not yet known but guessing at a lower figure than initially feared.

budget_items.topic: PFAS treatment bed-volume figures used in Tighe & Bond's cost analysis
budget_items.what_was_said: The resident argued the engineering firm used an incorrect, much higher bed-volume figure in their cost analysis table for treating Kedings water, which would overstate operating costs.

decisions.decision: Hold off signing the Verdantis fracture-trace/site-study agreement and first get pricing for actual test wells before proceeding.
Superintendent will compile a cost comparison of in-house vs. contracted water main work (using the Rolling Acres job) to help decide on future equipment purchases.
A private contractor doing a water tap/trench near Harbor Road was ordered to redig and redo the trench to the required depth after it was found too shallow.
Wait to see Tighe & Bond's cost proposal for the additional Kedings pH pilot study before deciding whether to push back on the DEP requirement.

minutes.summary: The Lunenburg Water District Commissioners reviewed and signed the warrant, approved prior minutes, and discussed a proposal from Verdantis/a hydrogeologist to investigate potential bedrock well sites near 361 Mass Path, deciding to get test-well pricing before signing any agreement. They also voted on a policy formalizing employee use of district vehicles for on-call response, received an update on the Rolling Acres water main replacement project (including a failed-then-repeated bacteria test and future equipment needs like a skid steer, sweeper and trailer), discussed a poorly-executed private trench dig on Harbor Road that had to be redone to proper depth, and heard extended public comment from a resident challenging the necessity and cost of an additional DEP-driven pilot study on treating water from the Kedings well.

why_it_matters: Any bedrock well investigation or added pilot study is a cost that would eventually be recovered through water rates, so the district is pricing before committing.
The pilot study concerns how the Kedings well's water gets treated, which bears on water quality and treatment costs passed to customers.
Equipment purchases weighed here (a pump, skid steer, trailer) feed into the district's capital spending and future water rates.
